reason: I'll start with the biceps, since the goal connects it to bending the elbow and the front of the arm has a space for it.
expectation: I expect the muscle cells to form or help build the biceps in the front of the arm; I'm not sure how they assemble.

alternatives.reason: Strengthening the front bone attachment also fits the goal, but I want to build the muscle first.

effect: The cells joined into long fibres forming the biceps, which bends the elbow; the bone still needs mineral.
reaction: Seeing how the cells form fibres and connect to the tendons was useful.
reason: I'll finish the front attachment by adding mineral, which the result says hardens the bone the tendon pulls on.
expectation: I expect the radius at the biceps attachment to become harder and stronger.

alternatives.reason: I could build the triceps next, but I want to finish the front first.

effect: Mineral filled spaces in the radius's bone fibres, completing the front goal while leaving the tendon and cartilage soft.
reaction: The distinction between hard bone and soft tendon was helpful.
reason: I'll build the triceps next, as the back muscle straightens the elbow.
expectation: I expect the cells to form a triceps between the back tendons, similar to how they formed the biceps.

alternatives.reason: I could mineralize the back bone first, but I'd rather build the muscle first as I did on the front.

effect: The triceps formed from the same kind of cells as the biceps, but its attachment behind the elbow makes it straighten the arm. The ulna still needs mineral.
reaction: The different effects of the two muscle positions make sense, though building the second muscle felt similar to the first.
reason: I'll add mineral to the back bone attachment to finish the remaining goal; it's the only gameplay action offered.
expectation: I expect mineral to harden the ulna where the triceps tendon attaches, as it did for the radius.

effect: The ulna gained mineral while the tendons and joint surfaces stayed soft, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: It matched the front-side result, so it felt a little repetitive.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the triceps after the biceps made the different effects of pulling in front of and behind the elbow clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding mineral to the second bone repeated the front-side action and felt predictable.

surprise.text: The same kind of muscle cells could help bend or straighten the elbow depending on their attachments.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary: the goals and pictures explained the muscles and bone mineral, although the compatible options supplied the pairings.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how other body parts work together, though I hope for less repetition than the second mineral fitting.
